title: add lightweight telemetry proxy for hackathon infra
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: during the company hackathon we prototyped several lightweight services that emit a lot of noisy telemetry to prod ingest pipelines. This PR adds a small, opt-in telemetry proxy intended for hackathon and experimentation environments to reduce noise and provide a single place to sample/strip PII before events reach the main pipeline. Design: the proxy runs as a tiny HTTP service in front of experimental services and performs configurable sampling, field redaction, and a fixed-rate buffer + forwarder. It is intentionally NOT intended for production workloads; defaults are safe and low-volume. Configuration examples and usage are embedded in the README. Checklist: - [x] implement proxy + minimal SDK shim - [x] add env-var toggles and feature-gate - [x] include Dockerfile and local run script - [x] add README and quickstart for hackathon teams - [x] run basic e2e in CI (smoke tests) How to run locally: export TELEMETRY_PROXY_ENABLED=1 && docker build -t telemetry-proxy . && docker run -e TELEMETRY_PROXY_ENABLED=1 -p 8080:8080 telemetry-proxy Notes: this proxy performs deterministic sampling and simple regex-based redaction (configurable). It emits a small health endpoint and basic Prometheus metrics. For anyone converting to a longer-lived integration, please open a follow-up RFC; this PR keeps scope intentionally small to avoid coupling with the main ingestion path. Related: links to internal hackathon guide and README in repo.
